TYPE CHECK: The candidate value is a chemical reagent used for alkylation, which matches the field definition.
SOURCE CHECK: The value "N-ethylmaleimide" is explicitly mentioned in the "In vivo ubiquitination assay" section as part of the lysis buffer.
TRUTH CHECK: The paper states that cell lysates were "lysed in lysis buffer containing 1% (w/v) SDS (PBS-SDS), and 10 mM N-ethylmaleimide." While this is part of the lysis for an in vivo ubiquitination assay (which is then analyzed by Western Blot), the "Protein digestion and affinity purification of ubiquitinated peptides" section (which feeds into the MS analysis) states that proteins were "reduced, alkylated, trypsinized," but does not explicitly name the alkylation reagent used for the MS samples. However, N-ethylmaleimide (NEM) is a standard alkylation reagent.
COMPLETENESS CHECK: The full set contains only this value.

Wait, looking closer at the "Protein digestion and affinity purification of ubiquitinated peptides" section: "The biotinylated-ubiquitinated proteins immobilized on beads were reduced, alkylated, trypsinized...". It does NOT name the reagent there.
The "In vivo ubiquitination assay" section mentions "10 mM N-ethylmaleimide" in the lysis buffer. This specific assay is followed by "resolved by SDS-PAGE followed by western blot analysis," NOT mass spectrometry.
The MS experiments (both the BirA-RNF8 screen and the NONO site mapping) use a different workflow. For the NONO site mapping: "The immunoprecipitated ubiquitinated NONO proteins were reduced, alkylated, trypsinized...". Again, the reagent is not named.

According to the rules: "A value that appears in the paper but ONLY in such an unrelated context is HALLUCINATED for the purpose of describing the MS experiment." The NEM is mentioned in the context of a Western Blot assay, not the MS sample preparation.
